name: Correct at every step, wrong at the end
def: No individual part of the system fails. Every department, every agent, every board process does exactly what it was designed to do, and the outcome is still wrong, with nobody positioned to own the gap.

instances.title: The Orchestration Crisis
instances.note: Multi-agent systems where every agent does its job and nobody is accountable between them.

instances.title: Every Department Did Its Job
instances.note: Every part functions correctly; the outcome is still wrong and nobody owns it.

instances.title: The KPI That Measured the Wrong Thing
instances.note: Digital services measurement that makes failure invisible while the dashboard stays green.

instances.title: The Decision Nobody Made
instances.note: Automated lending decisions accountable to no one.

instances.title: The Board That Didn’t Understand What It Had Approved
instances.note: AI accountability dispersing across the governance chain.

instances.title: The Leader Who Listened First
instances.note: Counter-example: mediation layers process out what matters before it reaches the decision-maker.

name: The dashboard stays green
def: Measurement and consultation substitute for genuine understanding. The organisation collects a number or a response, treats the collecting as the work, and never asks whether it changed anything.

instances.title: The number that tells you nothing
instances.note: Engagement scores measure the temperature of the room, not why it’s cold.

instances.title: The consultation that changed nothing
instances.note: Consultation designed to produce a record of having asked, not to change course.

instances.title: The Company That Measured What Mattered
instances.note: Organisations optimise for the first slide; the second slide rarely reaches the board.

instances.title: When the board asks the wrong question
instances.note: Engagement scores mistaken for people intelligence at board level.

instances.title: The data you already have and never read
instances.note: Years of qualitative data collected and treated as unanalysable.

instances.title: The Feedback Loop That Actually Worked
instances.note: Counter-example: visibility is the condition most feedback systems skip.

instances.title: The voice that never reaches the room
instances.note: The connective mechanism: intelligence degrades as it moves up the chain.

name: Built to be defensible, not to help
def: Institutional response systems for fraud, breach and cybersecurity are built to produce a record that the institution acted, not to close the exposure or protect the person living inside it.

card.title: How to Build Your Digital Fortress
How to Defend Your Identity from Theft and Impersonation

instances.title: Why the Victim Is Always Wrong
instances.note: Fraud response designed to protect the institution, burden placed on the victim.

instances.title: The fraud was an event. This is a condition.
instances.note: Recovery infrastructure built for institutional liability, not the person it’s meant to help.

instances.title: It Cannot Automate Trust
instances.note: Security advice that transfers the burden of defence to the least-equipped person.

instances.title: The company that knew and said nothing
instances.note: Breach disclosure designed to serve the institution managing it, not the person whose data was taken.

instances.title: It can be managed
instances.note: Governance built to document exposure, not close it.

instances.title: Crime with a support desk
instances.note: Criminal support infrastructure built to reduce friction better than legitimate response systems.

instances.title: Nobody Decided This Was Acceptable
instances.note: Stuxnet and the absence of updated international frameworks.

instances.title: They Already Have It
instances.note: Harvest-now-decrypt-later, active while migration hasn’t started.

name: Designed for the person who isn’t there
def: Systems are built around the capable, average, organised user, and fail exactly at the point where the person in front of them is least able to advocate for themselves.

instances.title: The Screen That Broke the Trust
instances.note: An NHS digital prescription system that worked exactly as designed, for a patient it wasn’t designed for.

instances.title: The Body That Remembers
instances.note: Systems built around emergency response, not the person living inside the risk every day after.

instances.title: The App That Actually Helped
instances.note: Counter-example: designed from what it feels like to manage a condition.

instances.title: While patients wait
instances.note: Proven AI diagnostics, blocked by funding and infrastructure from the people who need them most.

instances.title: The Last Person in the Queue
instances.note: Digital-by-default makes people who can’t use digital invisible.

instances.title: The Bin Hasn’t Changed (Only the Lorry)
instances.note: Digital-first layered onto analogue problems, indistinguishable from designed exclusion.

instances.title: Designing for the Person Who Isn’t Coping
instances.note: Design assumptions that fail precisely when the person is least able to advocate for themselves.

instances.title: The Question That Changed the Design
instances.note: “Who is this hardest for?” Almost never asked at the point it could change the outcome.

instances.title: The Land the Data Missed
instances.note: Precision agriculture designed for a farm most farmers don’t have.

instances.title: The Standard That Raised the Bar
instances.note: Counter-example: the curb-cut effect. Raising the floor for excluded users raises it for everyone.

name: The science works; access hasn’t followed
def: The scientific or clinical capability is real and proven. The barrier is who gets to it, at what cost, and on whose terms.

instances.title: The Body as a Lab
instances.note: In-vivo gene editing; governance decides who gets access.

instances.title: The Machine That Designs Medicines
instances.note: AI drug discovery outpacing the access question.

instances.title: What the Cold Chain Cannot Reach
instances.note: Biological medicine manufacturing concentrated in wealthy countries.

instances.title: Reading the Map Inside the Cell
instances.note: Spatial diagnostics confined to specialist centres.

instances.title: The instruction in the injection
instances.note: Personalised mRNA cancer vaccines, where personalisation itself is the access barrier.

instances.title: The bottleneck moved
instances.note: Drug discovery compressed to eighteen months; trial and regulatory pace hasn’t moved.

name: The science works; deployment infrastructure hasn’t followed
def: The engineering or technology is real and works at scale in principle. The barrier is the manufacturing capacity, regulatory pathway, or physical infrastructure needed to actually build and run it.
track: A new case, data centre energy demand colliding with grid capacity and local housing supply, is already being tracked for a future piece.

instances.title: Too Cheap to Meter, Too Slow to Build
instances.note: No SMR has been built on time or on budget yet.

instances.title: Three Days Earlier
instances.note: AI weather forecasting outruns the observational network it depends on.

instances.title: Coverage Is Not Access
instances.note: Satellite coverage reaches billions; subscribers number in the millions.

instances.title: What gets funded in space
instances.note: Commercial orbital platforms changing who decides what science gets funded.

instances.title: It Remembers What Shape to Be
instances.note: Shape-memory alloys constrained by regulatory and manufacturing scale-up.

instances.title: The Science Is Not the Problem
instances.note: Self-healing concrete, deployed since 2011, invisible to procurement that prices only the initial build.

instances.title: Twenty Watts
instances.note: The brain does in 20 watts what GPU-based AI vision burns thousands of times more energy to match.

instances.title: The Error is the Point
instances.note: Quantum error correction confirmed; the cryptographic migration hasn’t started.

instances.title: They Already Have It
instances.note: Post-quantum standards published in 2024; most organisations still have no cryptographic inventory. Also in “Built to be defensible, not to help.”

name: The permanent record you didn’t choose
def: Data about a person is captured once and becomes a durable, portable record used to make decisions about them, with no mechanism for the person to see it, correct it, or reclaim it.

card.title: How to Manage Your Algorithmic Reputation
How to Shape Your Networked Self

instances.title: The Thing You Gave Away for Free
instances.note: Personal data shared online creates a permanent, portable record that can’t be reclaimed.

instances.title: The Anticipatory Trap
instances.note: The model built of you is owned by the platform, not by you.

instances.title: Permanent, Portable, Wrong
instances.note: Data profiles determine credit, job screening and insurance terms before the decision is even made.

instances.title: Sovereign is Not a Postcode
instances.note: Datacentre location is not the same as control over the data in it.

name: Engineered compulsion
def: Attention and agency are captured by design, not accident: mechanisms borrowed from behavioural psychology that produce a compulsion the person experiences as their own failing.

instances.title: The Campfire Problem
instances.note: The evolutionary pull to share attention, captured and redirected by design.

instances.title: The Stage With Too Many Actors
instances.note: Digital environments systematically exceed finite attention capacity.

instances.title: Technically Present
instances.note: Inattentional blindness as a designed operating condition, not a concentration problem.

instances.title: A Reflex That Was Installed
instances.note: The compulsion to check your phone, engineered on slot-machine mechanics.

instances.title: Boredom Was the Doorway
instances.note: The absence of boredom is the first thing the design took away from children.

instances.title: Why Helpful Isn’t the Same as Good
instances.note: Technically helpful, entirely wrong: a voice assistant answering a child about death.

name: The application serves the pipeline metric, not the candidate
def: Recruitment and hiring technology is optimised for the volume and manageability of the process on the organisation’s side. The candidate’s chance of being seen by a person is not the thing it was built to protect.
track: Two further cases, correlated rejection across employers using the same screening model, and CV-screening that reads a career gap for childcare or caring like any other gap, are already being tracked for future pieces.

instances.title: Apply. Wait. Disappear.
instances.note: Easy Apply generates volume that serves recruiter pipeline metrics, not candidate chances.

instances.title: The Application That Went Nowhere
instances.note: The process structurally redesigned to serve the organisation, not the candidate experience.
